svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: The replication cell grid, seen from one session
What a session holds is recomputed from geometry every frame: an anchor, a radius and one bit per cell of its window. Nothing is stored per entity.
a
1 · What the session holds
known(s, e) ⟺ |a − v̂ₑ| ≤ R′ and cell(v̂ₑ) is delivered
The window is (2h + 1) cells per axis, h = ⌈R′/c⌉ + 2.
Cells are delivered nearest first, under the enter budget:
a hatched cell is in range but not sent yet, so its
entities are not held yet. The geometry stays exact.
2 · The anchor moves: sweep the crescent
Only cells straddling either sphere are swept.
The anchor moves only past a slack of min(R′/48, c/2),
so a still or slow viewer costs nothing. The move here is
exaggerated. A move of more than one cell is a teleport:
a RESET, and the view is delivered again.
update, no test
enter
leave
h_A
3 · This tick's events, cell by cell
was = the old v̂ held, is = the new v̂ held.
A blue cell (inside the sphere, delivered in both windows)
needs no test. v̂ moves only past the slack h_A, so a
mover whose motion segment still holds makes no event.
A cell change files the event under both cells.
anchor
interior cell
straddling cell: tested per entity
in range, not delivered yet
held entity
not held
enter
leave
Cells: side c = ReplicationCellM. Here R′ = 3c, the rule of thumb, so h = 5 and the window is 11 × 11. In a deep (3D) grid the same holds with cubes, spheres and a shell.
